letter.to: To the bearer -- by hand, this Sunday morning
lines: Mr. Vesper is dead at his own hearth, certified of his heart before the coroner could properly sit.
I will not trouble you with all my reasons -- the sealed letter he left for me is reason enough, and the telephone call before it.
The household is five guests and a housekeeper, and every one of them slept badly. Sergeant Hollis holds the door; I have paid for your eye.
Come before the will is read. Look closely. Tell me what the hall says, then the parlour. Begin at the beginning of the night.

prologue.title: The House
body: Three storeys over a cellar: entrance hall and parlour to the front, kitchen behind, study beside. Five beds above, a studio under the roof, and a cot below.
The storm took the power at 10:47. The hall clock keeps the hour of it still.

prologue.title: Your Instruments
body: A magnifier -- for films, prints, petals and other small refusals of the truth.
A sketchbook that fills itself: every clue you touch is drawn into it with my notes -- Clues, People, Timeline, Threads.
A Think button. It nudges, it presses, it nearly answers. No shame in it; the house is dark and the suspects are many.
A UV torch, packed away for a later act. The kitchen, stairs, bedrooms, attic and cellar likewise.
prologue.footnote: Tap a room on the map to walk it. Drag the walls to look along them. Tap anything that draws your eye.

prologue.title: Take Up the Case
body: Sergeant Hollis waits at the door with the storm at his back. He will say his piece, then the house is yours.
Read the hall first. The parlour stays sealed until you can tell him what the hall told you. Then the parlour -- and the night's whole arithmetic.
When you can name the poison, the vessel, the fire and the door, say so. That is Act I, done.
